ds: Breaking up cash or other value into amounts kept below reporting, identification or internal review thresholds, often using many deposits, branches, accounts or individuals. It is mainly a placement technique and is commonly paired with rapid onward movement of funds.

src.t: FATF, Money Laundering Typologies and Methods (general placement guidance)
FinCEN, Guidance on structuring and Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) reporting (general)
AUSTRAC, Guidance on structuring and threshold transaction reports (general)

cn.rt: Sub-threshold cash deposits at branch and ATM-linked flows into accounts, term deposit placement, with rapid digital onward movement.

rat: Sub-threshold cash deposits across branches, ATMs and agents.

ind.n: Repeated cash deposits just below reporting threshold
ind.cx: Multiple cash deposits or exchanges sized just under a regulatory reporting or internal review threshold over a short period.
ind.fp: Customers with stable habits (e.g. fixed daily takings or standard float sizes) can legitimately generate similar amounts.
ind.ds: Repeated cash deposits kept just under a reporting, identification or monitoring threshold.
ind.cn: Cash deposits just below reporting or identification threshold

ind.n: Same-day deposits across multiple branches or ATMs
ind.cx: Cash is paid in at several branches, ATMs or agents within hours, with total value well above the amount at any one location.
ind.fp: Travelling workers or customers with several workplaces may use many locations.
ind.ds: Cash is deposited in several locations, channels or accounts on the same day or over a short period so that no single deposit stands out.
ind.cn: Cash deposits split across branches, ATMs or accounts

ind.n: Multiple depositors paying into one account
ind.cx: Several unrelated individuals make cash deposits into the same account, often in similar amounts and at similar times.
ind.fp: Collections for clubs, rent, fundraising or family contributions may fit.
ind.ds: Numerous unconnected individuals make deposits into the same account, often in similar amounts or within short windows.
ind.cn: Many unrelated depositors paying into one account

ind.n: Rapid onward movement after cash credits
ind.cx: Funds credited in cash are quickly transferred out, withdrawn elsewhere or used for purchases leaving a low balance.
ind.fp: Customers paying bills or suppliers on receipt of cash may do the same.
ind.ds: Cash deposited is quickly withdrawn or transferred onward, including to another location or to unhosted wallets.

ind.n: Customer reacts to reporting or ID requirements
ind.cx: Customer reduces a transaction, splits it, or leaves when asked for ID, source of funds or told a report may be filed.
ind.fp: Privacy concerns or lack of documents with the customer may explain some cases.
ind.ds: Customer reduces a transaction, splits it, or leaves when asked for ID, source of funds or told a report may be filed.

ind.n: Deposit volumes inconsistent with customer profile
ind.cx: Cash volumes far exceed expected activity for the customer's declared occupation, income or business.
ind.fp: Windfalls, asset sales or seasonal income may be genuine.
ind.ds: Turnover or volumes materially exceed what the customer's declared occupation, income, age or circumstances would support.
ind.cn: Account activity inconsistent with declared occupation or income

ind.n: Frequent purchase of monetary instruments in small amounts
ind.cx: Multiple money orders, drafts, prepaid cards or cheques purchased with cash in sub-threshold amounts.
ind.fp: Some customers lack bank accounts and use instruments for rent or bills.
ind.ds: Multiple money orders, drafts, prepaid cards or cheques purchased with cash in sub-threshold amounts.

ind.cx: Cash arrives in unusual bundles, rubber-banded small notes, or mixed denominations inconsistent with the stated source.
ind.fp: Retail cash is often in small notes; condition varies by source.
ind.ds: Cash arrives in unusual bundles, rubber-banded small notes, or mixed denominations inconsistent with the stated source.

ctl.ds: Aggregates cash and other activity by customer, related party, account, branch, channel and day so that splitting across touchpoints cannot evade review, supported by a single customer view. It gives analysts a holistic picture of exposure.
Detects repeated transactions placed just below reporting or approval limits, tuned by band and window per segment. It counters deliberate splitting designed to avoid scrutiny.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

ctl.n: Fan-in, fan-out and funnel account detection
ctl.ds: Detects accounts receiving from many unrelated senders, or sending to many beneficiaries, followed by consolidation or onward movement. It surfaces collector, funnel and mule structures.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.
Alerts when inflows are quickly moved out with little retained balance, including cash-in fast-out and rapid conversion or cash-out. It reveals accounts used as conduits for layering.

ctl.n: Specialist investigation and suspicious activity reporting
ctl.ds: Trained analysts investigate alerts with typology playbooks, document rationale and file reports where suspicion is formed, with prompt reporting to the competent authority. It converts alerts into actionable intelligence.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.
Provides a simple internal reporting channel and feedback loop so front-line staff can escalate observations, pressure and cash-handling anomalies. It turns staff observations into cases for review.

Compares actual activity with the customer's declared profile, history and peers and alerts on material or trend-breaking deviation, usually as a contextual signal. It catches change that rules on fixed thresholds miss.

Obtains and tests documentary evidence of where the money for a transaction, deposit or capital injection comes from, particularly when value exceeds thresholds or the customer profile. It reduces the chance that illicit proceeds are accepted without explanation.
